instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Put a rimmed baking sheet on the middle rack.

Make the chimichurri first. Finely chop 2 packed cups of parsley leaves and tender stems, mince the shallot and the garlic, and put them in a bowl. Stir in 1/2 cup olive oil, 1/4 cup red wine vinegar, the oregano and 1/2 tsp salt.

Take the outer leaves off each cauliflower and trim the stem flat. Cut each head in half from top to stem, then cut a slab about 1 1/2 inches thick from the middle of each half. Keep some stem on each one so it holds together. Save the leftover cauliflower for another meal.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 2 of the cauliflower slabs and cook for 5 minutes, until deep golden underneath.
Flip them and sprinkle with a little of the remaining salt. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, then transfer them to the hot baking sheet.
Wipe the skillet if it's dark, heat the other 2 tbsp olive oil, and cook the last 2 slabs the same way.
Put all 4 slabs on the baking sheet and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until the stems are tender when you poke them with a fork.
Taste the chimichurri. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the chimichurri over the cauliflower. Pass the red pepper flakes at the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: Inspired Taste is the lead (steaks about 1 1/2 inches thick seared in a skillet, finished in a 400°F oven, with a parsley and red wine vinegar chimichurri), but it has only 14 ratings, so this is a fallback lead; no version with 20 or more ratings could be read. Delish Knowledge roasts the steaks with no sear and adds mint; Cadry's Kitchen blends a cilantro sauce. The red pepper flakes from the lead's chimichurri go on the side. The lead makes 2 steaks, so this uses two heads for 4.
